p2_b2.ocr: Fuzzy sets and fuzzy numbers Fuzzy set theory was introduced in 1965 by Zadeh [51] to handle uncertainty due to imprecise or vague information. A fuzzy set A = {(x, μA(x)) | x X} is a set of ordered pairs, where X is a subset of the real numbers R and μA(x) is a membership function that assigns to each objective x a score ranging from zero to one [52]. Fuzzy set theory is integrated into the pairwise com- parison matrices of the AHP.
